newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BANKS' Q1 OP PROFIT DOUBLED - ASSOCIATION.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BANKS' Q1 OP PROFIT DOUBLED - ASSOCIATION.

text.p: Finnish banks' aggregate operating profit after credit losses doubled in the first quarter 1997 on the same period the previous year, the Finnish Bankers' Association said on Tuesday.
The banks' combined operating profit in January-March was almost 1.7 billion markka.
"The improvement of the profit was due to lower credit losses, increased income and reduced expenses," the association said.
Aggregate credit losses fell to 447 million markka from 930 million in the same period last year. Non-performing receivables fell to 9.6 billion markka from 15.3 billion at end-March 1996.
Net income from financial operations was 2.7 billion markka and more or less unchanged from the first quarter last year.
Banks' total income grew 145 million markka to 5.4 billion markka.

The figures covered banking groups Merita Oy , the cooperative banks around OKOBANK , state-owned Postipankki Oy, the savings banks, state-controlled Yrityspankki Skop Oy, Alandsbanken and Interbank, the association said. -- Eeva Prunnila, Helsinki newsroom + 358 - 9 - 680 50 248
